judgement.impact: Screen-reader user hears only 'rating' and cannot know the product is rated 4.3 stars.
User hears only generic badge and cannot know the product is advertised as 20% off on sale.
The user hears only 'based on 212 reviews' and cannot learn the 4-out-of-5 star rating that sighted users see.
The user cannot tell what the first product thumbnail shows and cannot distinguish this view from the other gallery images.
User cannot tell what product view the second thumbnail shows and misses the visual detail a sighted user gets.
The screen-reader user cannot tell which colour Option 1 represents or that it is currently selected, so cannot knowingly choose the desired colour.
The user cannot know that Option 3 is the blue colour and cannot confidently select the intended colour variant.
User cannot tell that this button selects the beige colour and cannot reliably choose the intended colour variant.
Blind user cannot tell that Standard is the currently selected size and cannot verify their size choice before purchase.
The sighted user sees only a light outline shape with no product detail, so a screen-reader user who ignores it as decorative loses no information or ability to act.
The user cannot tell the product is in stock and available because the green colour meaning is announced only as "status".
User cannot tell R1,599.00 is the crossed-out original price and may mistake it for the current price instead of R1,249.00.
Screen-reader user hears the lump-sum prices but cannot know the item can be paid in 4 instalments of R312.25.
Screen-reader user does not know the sale price expires in about 2 hours and may miss the discounted price.
The user cannot know the button saves to wishlist and hears Close instead, so they will avoid it or expect it to close something.
The screen-reader user hears only More and cannot identify or activate the link as the visible Compare action.
